description: Agent Hiring: submit a candidate’s availability or start commitment with the brief’s timeline: the commitment with the candidate, the day it was stated, the day the candidate can start, the capacity stated in hours or days a week, the completion day committed to and each stretch of unavailability; the brief with the days work starts and is due, the capacity it needs and the total hours it estimates. The signed report gives the commitment and the brief, the start and the completion against the brief’s days, the capacity against the capacity needed, and the hours the commitment holds recomputed as its weekly hours times the days from its start to its completion, less each stretch of unavailability, over seven, against the brief’s estimate, and counts them, and names a divergent commitment: a start after the brief’s start, a completion after its due day, less capacity than it needs, fewer hours than it estimates and a completion before the start; then another capacity unit, unavailability inside the work and a commitment stated after its own start, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No start, no completion or due day, or no capacity on either side leaves the commitment unverified. Days read as days and hours compare to the hundredth. An availability commitment is a document read against the brief’s timeline: wever_capacity-workload-check and the other Agent Capacity checks read the operational capacity metrics of a running system, such as the work in hand against a stated limit, while the availability check reads a candidate’s start, capacity and completion as stated against the dates and the hours the brief sets. Verdict hire_availability_divergent, hire_availability_partial, hire_availability_unverified or hire_availability_consistent. POST /api/hire-availability-check. Reads the hiring paperwork supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads consistency between documents only, with no judgment of whether a candidate is good, qualified in substance or worth hiring, no background check, no contact with referees or issuers, no verification with outside sources and no employment-law advice, and the paperwork stays in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Hiring reads supplied hiring paperwork for consistency between documents: a hiring brief, a credential record, a portfolio or past-work record, a reference, a rate quote, an engagement contract, an availability commitment and a payment setup. Beside it, wever_post-job, wever_accept-job and the other tools of the intent job kit are the execution layer that posts, accepts and settles jobs, and wever_workorder-create and the other wever_workorder tools and wever_agent-work-order-exchange are the action layer that creates, funds, delivers and releases work orders, while this family moves nothing and executes nothing and only reads paperwork before anything is committed; wever_agent-escrow-lite holds and releases escrowed funds, and escrow stays there. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-hiring-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-hiring/.
